Q000588:
Why this is correct:
Long-running work shouldn't block the request. Accept the upload, return a request ID, and process asynchronously, letting the client poll or receive a notification.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Blocking WebSocket: still waits.
• 15-minute synchronous Lambda: exceeds API limits.
• Synchronous API call: times out.

Key takeaway: long jobs → asynchronous request/response.
Q000589:
Why this is correct:
API Gateway REST integrations time out at 29 seconds by default. A slower backend call returns 504.

Why the other options are wrong:
• High reserved concurrency: doesn't slow calls.
• High memory: speeds startup.
• DynamoDB throttling: would show errors, possibly, but the timeout is the gateway limit.

Key takeaway: 504 from API Gateway → integration timeout.
Q000591:
Why this is correct:
Publishing v2 as a new version or stage while keeping v1 running avoids breaking existing clients.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Overwrite in place: breaks clients.
• Delete old API: breaks clients.
• Change only Lambda: still breaking.

Key takeaway: breaking changes → versioned APIs.
Q000592:
Why this is correct:
Unit tests with a local test framework and mocked AWS SDK calls test business logic quickly without deploying.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Timeout: unrelated.
• Deploy and invoke manually: slow, not unit tests.
• X-Ray in production: not testing.

Key takeaway: unit tests → mocks.
Q000593:
Why this is correct:
A FIFO queue preserves order, and content-based deduplication prevents duplicates within the 5-minute window.

Why the other options are wrong:
• FIFO with 14-day retention: retention doesn't deduplicate.
• Standard with short timeout: no ordering.
• Standard with DLQ: no ordering.

Key takeaway: ordered and deduplicated → FIFO + deduplication.
Q000594:
Why this is correct:
The SDK's built-in retries with exponential backoff handle transient throttling automatically.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Disable SSL validation: insecure.
• Poll CloudWatch Logs: unrelated.
• Terminate on exceptions: not resilient.

Key takeaway: throttling → retries with backoff.
Q000595:
Why this is correct:
Kinesis Data Streams ingests at high scale and lets multiple independent consumers read the same data, with replay.

Why the other options are wrong:
• SQS Standard: each message consumed once.
• SNS: no storage or replay.
• SQS FIFO: throughput limits and single consumption.

Key takeaway: multiple consumers + replay → Kinesis.
Q000596:
Why this is correct:
Throughput exceptions with spare total capacity point to skewed partition keys creating a hot shard. Use higher-cardinality keys.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Retention: unrelated.
• Enhanced fan-out: consumer side.
• Shard count limit: not the error.

Key takeaway: hot shards → better partition keys.
Q000598:
Why this is correct:
An EventBridge event pattern can match the bucket name and a key suffix of .csv, so the rule fires only for CSV objects.

Why the other options are wrong:
• S3 emits only .csv: filtering belongs in the rule.
• Two functions: wasteful.
• CloudWatch alarms: not event routing.

Key takeaway: filter events with patterns.
Q000599:
Why this is correct:
EventBridge offers content-based routing rules to many targets and a schema registry for event discovery.

Why the other options are wrong:
• SQS ordering: not routing.
• SNS filtering: fewer targets and no schema registry.
• Direct Connect: networking.

Key takeaway: event routing → EventBridge.
Q000602:
Why this is correct:
A VPC-attached Lambda uses private IPs. Without a route to a NAT gateway or VPC endpoints, it can't reach public AWS services like DynamoDB.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Low memory: unrelated.
• ElastiCache SG: affects ElastiCache, not other services.
• Missing DynamoDB permissions: would show AccessDenied.

Key takeaway: VPC Lambda needs NAT or endpoints.
Q000603:
Why this is correct:
Reserved concurrency of 20 caps the function's concurrent executions at 20.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Provisioned concurrency: pre-warms, doesn't cap.
• Alarm after 20 invocations: not concurrency.
• Visibility timeout: SQS setting.

Key takeaway: cap concurrency → reserved concurrency.
Q000604:
Why this is correct:
Provisioned concurrency keeps environments initialized, avoiding cold starts during traffic spikes.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Timeout: unrelated.
• X-Ray: observation.
• Reserved concurrency: caps, doesn't warm.

Key takeaway: cold starts → provisioned concurrency.
Q000605:
Why this is correct:
A Lambda extension runs alongside the function and can capture telemetry and logs and forward them to third-party platforms.

Why the other options are wrong:
• More memory: unrelated.
• Subscription filter: works but adds a separate pipeline; extensions integrate directly.
• Layer with SDK only: no lifecycle integration.

Key takeaway: telemetry agents → Lambda extensions.
Q000607:
Why this is correct:
SQS and Kinesis use event source mappings where Lambda polls the source.

Why the other options are wrong:
• SNS and S3: push.
• EventBridge and Step Functions: push/invoke.
• API Gateway and ALB: synchronous invoke.

Key takeaway: poll-based sources → SQS, Kinesis, DynamoDB Streams.
Q000609:
Why this is correct:
An on-failure destination (such as an EventBridge bus) receives the original event, response, and error details for async invocations.

Why the other options are wrong:
• X-Ray: traces.
• DLQ: event only, fewer details.
• Subscription filter: logs.

Key takeaway: failure context → on-failure destinations.
Q000610:
Why this is correct:
SAM CLI (sam local invoke) runs the function in a Lambda-like container locally.

Why the other options are wrong:
• CloudTrail, Config, Synthetics: not local testing.

Key takeaway: local Lambda testing → SAM CLI.
Q000612:
Why this is correct:
DynamoDB Streams with a Lambda event source mapping processes every item change in order per item.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Capacity alarms: not changes.
• Scanning every minute: costly and misses intermediate states.
• S3 backups: unrelated.

Key takeaway: react to table changes → Streams.
Q000613:
Why this is correct:
Initializing clients and static data outside the handler runs once per execution environment and is reused across invocations.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Disable role: nonsense.
• Longer timeout: doesn't speed startup.
• Less memory: slower.

Key takeaway: reuse initialization outside the handler.
Q000614:
Why this is correct:
Kinesis Data Streams with a Lambda consumer processes sensor data in real time, and extended retention allows replay.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Nightly Glue: not real time.
• Glacier: archive.
• SNS only: no storage or replay.

Key takeaway: real-time stream processing → Kinesis + Lambda.
Q000617:
Why this is correct:
A strongly consistent read (ConsistentRead=true) on the base table returns the latest committed value.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Eventually consistent: may be stale.
• GSI reads: eventually consistent.
• Scan: not the point and costly.

Key takeaway: latest value → strongly consistent reads.
Q000618:
Why this is correct:
GSIs are updated asynchronously, so they support only eventually consistent reads.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Cost reasons: not why.
• LSIs replaced: no.
• Deprecated: no.

Key takeaway: GSI reads are eventually consistent.
Q000620:
Why this is correct:
Filters apply after items are read, so a Scan still consumes capacity for every item scanned. Use Query with a key or a GSI.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Invalid syntax: no.
• More write capacity: unrelated.
• Scan doesn't support filters: it does.

Key takeaway: filters don't reduce read cost.
Q000621:
Why this is correct:
A Query on CustomerId with OrderDate BETWEEN the two dates reads only the matching items, sorted.

Why the other options are wrong:
• BatchGetItem with only partition key: needs full keys.
• Scan with filter: reads everything.
• GetItem per date: many calls and needs exact keys.

Key takeaway: key-based ranges → Query.
Q000622:
Why this is correct:
A GSI can use any attributes as keys and can be added anytime. An LSI must share the table's partition key and be created with the table.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Consistency swapped: LSIs support strong consistency.
• Throughput swapped: GSIs have their own capacity.
• Same feature: different.

Key takeaway: GSI = flexible; LSI = same partition key, at creation.
Q000624:
Why this is correct:
A sparse GSI keyed on Status contains only items that have the attribute, so querying returned orders reads a small index.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Separate S3 store: complicates data.
• Status as sort key: changes the primary key.
• Scheduled Scan: costly.

Key takeaway: find a small subset → sparse index.
Q000626:
Why this is correct:
The low-level API wraps each value with a type descriptor. Numbers use N with the value as a string: {"N": "42"}.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Bare value: missing type.
• S type: string, not number.
• Number key: invalid descriptor.

Key takeaway: low-level DynamoDB types need descriptors.
Q000627:
Why this is correct:
A TTL attribute with an expiration timestamp lets DynamoDB delete items automatically at no write cost.

Why the other options are wrong:
• On-demand: billing mode.
• Scheduled scan and delete: costly.
• Streams only: no deletion.

Key takeaway: automatic expiry → TTL.
Q000628:
Why this is correct:
Point-in-time recovery restores a table to any second within the last 35 days.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Global Tables: replication.
• Streams: change capture.
• Monthly on-demand backups: coarse.

Key takeaway: any point in 35 days → PITR.
Q000629:
Why this is correct:
ElastiCache as a cache-aside layer serves repeated reads from memory, cutting DynamoDB reads and latency (DAX is another option).

Why the other options are wrong:
• Auto scaling: doesn't cut repeated reads.
• Streams: change capture.
• Write capacity: reads are the issue.

Key takeaway: repeated reads → cache.
Q000631:
Why this is correct:
Streaming changes into OpenSearch provides full-text search with typo tolerance and relevance ranking.

Why the other options are wrong:
• S3 for all: no search.
• Scan with contains(): slow and no relevance.
• More read capacity: doesn't add search.

Key takeaway: full-text search → OpenSearch.
Q000632:
Why this is correct:
Adding data nodes and revisiting shard count and size relieves resource pressure and improves query performance.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Single primary shard: limits parallelism.
• No replicas: hurts availability and reads.
• One index with no rotation: grows unbounded.

Key takeaway: OpenSearch performance → capacity + sharding strategy.
Q000634:
Why this is correct:
A Cognito identity pool that trusts the user pool exchanges tokens for temporary credentials mapped to a scoped IAM role.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Embedded access key: insecure.
• Lambda authorizer on S3: doesn't exist.
• IAM user per app user: unmanageable.

Key takeaway: app users → AWS credentials via identity pools.
Q000635:
Why this is correct:
SAML 2.0 federation supports corporate identity providers, and web identity federation via an IAM OIDC provider supports OIDC providers.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Anonymous bucket access: insecure.
• Mirror IAM users: unmanageable.
• Root credentials: never.

Key takeaway: external identities → SAML or OIDC federation.
Q000637:
Why this is correct:
A Lambda authorizer receives the token from the configured header. A missing Bearer prefix or wrong header makes validation fail.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Custom domain: unrelated.
• Reserved concurrency: unrelated.
• Versioned bucket: unrelated.

Key takeaway: check the token source and format first.
Q000639:
Why this is correct:
The target role's trust policy must trust the caller's execution role (and the caller needs sts:AssumeRole permission).

Why the other options are wrong:
• Reserved concurrency: unrelated.
• BasicExecutionRole on target: unrelated.
• Bucket encryption: unrelated.

Key takeaway: AssumeRole needs trust.
Q000641:
Why this is correct:
Permissions boundaries let developers create roles while capping the maximum permissions those roles can have.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Groups: users only.
• Resource-based policies: grant access to resources.
• Root SCP only: account-wide, not per role.

Key takeaway: safe delegation → permissions boundaries.
Q000642:
Why this is correct:
An IAM condition on dynamodb:LeadingKeys restricts each tenant's credentials to items with their partition key.

Why the other options are wrong:
• PITR: backups.
• Application-only token validation: no enforcement in AWS.
• Streams: change capture.

Key takeaway: tenant row isolation in DynamoDB → LeadingKeys.
Q000644:
Why this is correct:
Service A's task role signs requests with SigV4, and the API method uses IAM authorization to allow only that role.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Shared keys: insecure.
• No authorization: insecure.
• Unauthenticated Cognito role: not service identity.

Key takeaway: service-to-service auth → IAM auth + SigV4.
Q000645:
Why this is correct:
mTLS authenticates at the transport level but needs a CA and certificate management. IRSA with SigV4 uses IAM identities for AWS-style authorization.

Why the other options are wrong:
• IRSA not on EKS: it's for EKS.
• Identical: different layers.
• mTLS needs no certificates: it does.

Key takeaway: mTLS vs. IAM identity: different tradeoffs.
Q000647:
Why this is correct:
An explicit Deny in any applicable policy overrides any Allow, so the action is denied.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Group creation order: irrelevant.
• Allowed because one allows: deny wins.
• Independent evaluation: all policies combine.

Key takeaway: explicit deny always wins.
Q000648:
Why this is correct:
A bucket policy denying requests when aws:SecureTransport is false blocks HTTP access.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Transfer Acceleration: speed.
• SSE-S3: at rest.
• Versioning: data protection.

Key takeaway: enforce HTTPS → SecureTransport deny.
Q000651:
Why this is correct:
ACM Private CA issues private certificates for internal mTLS between services.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Cognito: user auth.
• Public ACM: public names.
• Secrets Manager: secrets storage.

Key takeaway: internal certificates → Private CA.
Q000652:
Why this is correct:
AWS RAM can share a Private CA with other accounts so they can issue certificates from it.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Copying the private key: impossible and unsafe.
• SCPs: don't share resources.
• Bucket policies: unrelated.

Key takeaway: share a CA across accounts → RAM.
Q000654:
Why this is correct:
Client-side encryption with a local key encrypts data before upload, so AWS never sees plaintext.

Why the other options are wrong:
• AWS owned key: server side.
• SSE-KMS managed key: server side.
• SSE-S3: server side.

Key takeaway: never plaintext in AWS → client-side encryption.
Q000655:
Why this is correct:
Envelope encryption uses GenerateDataKey to get a data key, encrypts the file locally, and stores the encrypted data key alongside it.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Encrypt whole file: 4 KB limit.
• Disable rotation: unrelated.
• Store key material locally: not possible with KMS.

Key takeaway: large data → envelope encryption.
Q000656:
Why this is correct:
AWS managed keys rotate automatically. Customer managed key rotation is optional and configurable.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Customer sets both schedules: no.
• Managed keys never rotate: they do.
• CMKs can't rotate: they can.

Key takeaway: managed = automatic; CMK = optional.
Q000657:
Why this is correct:
Specify an EC2 key pair at launch and connect with its private key.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Root password: no.
• Public bucket: exposes key.
• KMS key pair in user data: exposes key.

Key takeaway: SSH access → key pairs.
Q000659:
Why this is correct:
Certificates from a private CA fail unless clients trust the CA chain. Install the private CA root in clients' trust stores.

Why the other options are wrong:
• EC2 key pair: unrelated.
• Automatic rotation without notice: not the main cause.
• Public trust anchor: private CAs aren't publicly trusted.

Key takeaway: private certs need client trust.
Q000662:
Why this is correct:
Processing PHI on AWS requires a Business Associate Addendum with AWS and using only HIPAA-eligible services, plus appropriate configuration.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Cognito for storage: nonsense.
• Default encryption only: insufficient.
• Versioning: not compliance.

Key takeaway: PHI → BAA + eligible services.
Q000664:
Why this is correct:
Lambda environment variables can be encrypted with a customer managed KMS key, controlling who can decrypt them.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Can't use CMKs: they can.
• Hardcode: worse.
• Disable encryption: not allowed and insecure.

Key takeaway: sensitive env vars → CMK encryption.
Q000666:
Why this is correct:
Secrets Manager provides native rotation templates for database credentials.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Identical rotation: Parameter Store lacks it.
• Can't store DB credentials: it can.
• Parameter Store cheaper: but lacks rotation.

Key takeaway: rotating credentials → Secrets Manager.
Q000667:
Why this is correct:
If the secret uses a customer managed key, the task role needs kms:Decrypt through the key policy.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Container Insights: unrelated.
• Launch type: unrelated.
• Rotation disabled: doesn't block reads.

Key takeaway: secret reads with CMKs need key access.
Q000668:
Why this is correct:
CloudWatch Logs data protection policies detect and mask sensitive data such as SSNs in log events.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Composite alarms: alerts.
• Query caching: no.
• KMS encryption: at rest, not masking.

Key takeaway: mask sensitive log data → data protection policies.
Q000669:
Why this is correct:
Role-based masking in the application shows full SSNs only to authorized roles and masked values to others.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Admin for all: violates policy.
• Bucket encryption: doesn't mask displays.
• Masked copies without controls: still exposed.

Key takeaway: field-level visibility → app-layer masking.
Q000670:
Why this is correct:
PostgreSQL row-level security policies filter rows by tenant context, isolating tenants in a shared database.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Backups: unrelated.
• IAM DB auth alone: authenticates, doesn't isolate rows.
• Multi-AZ: availability.

Key takeaway: shared-DB tenant isolation → RLS.
Q000671:
Why this is correct:
A pool model is cheaper but needs strict tenant isolation controls. A silo model isolates tenants best at higher cost.

Why the other options are wrong:
• No difference: silo is stronger.
• Pool gives automatic per-tenant keys: no.
• Silo weaker: no.

Key takeaway: pool vs. silo = cost vs. isolation.
Q000672:
Why this is correct:
A separate customer managed KMS key per tenant limits the impact of a compromised key to that tenant.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Same password: shared blast radius.
• Shared managed key: shared blast radius.
• No encryption: unacceptable.

Key takeaway: per-tenant keys contain blast radius.
Q000678:
Why this is correct:
AppConfig validators (a JSON Schema or a Lambda function) on the configuration profile reject invalid configurations before deployment.

Why the other options are wrong:
• CodeBuild validation: outside AppConfig.
• Permissions boundary: unrelated.
• Bake-time alarm: after deployment starts.

Key takeaway: validate config before deploy → AppConfig validators.
Q000679:
Why this is correct:
sam build writes built artifacts to the .aws-sam/build directory.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Git objects: no.
• Overwrites sources: no.
• CloudTrail bucket: no.

Key takeaway: SAM build output → .aws-sam/build.
Q000681:
Why this is correct:
Container settings such as image, CPU, memory, ports, and environment are defined in the ECS task definition.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Dockerfile CMD: startup command only.
• Route table: networking.
• ECR policy: repository access.

Key takeaway: ECS runtime config → task definition.
Q000682:
Why this is correct:
An AppConfig deployment strategy with growth rate and bake time rolls out gradually, and an alarm monitor rolls back automatically.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Lambda alias weights: code, not config.
• Stage variables: API settings.
• AppSpec hooks: CodeDeploy.

Key takeaway: gradual config rollout → AppConfig strategy + alarms.
Q000684:
Why this is correct:
A mock integration returns responses defined in API Gateway, so frontend teams can build against the API before backends exist.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Lambda proxy: needs the function.
• HTTP integration: needs a backend.
• AWS service integration: calls real services.

Key takeaway: API before backend → mock integration.
Q000686:
Why this is correct:
Run sam build then sam deploy, which creates a CloudFormation change set you can review before updating the stack.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Delete and recreate: disruptive.
• Manual console changes: drift.
• sam local start-api: local only.

Key takeaway: update SAM stacks → build + deploy.
Q000687:
Why this is correct:
Invoking the function with a sample S3 event JSON (for example, from sam local generate-event) tests its logic realistically.

Why the other options are wrong:
• No payload: logic can't run.
• Change trigger: tests something else.
• Delete notifications: unnecessary.

Key takeaway: test with realistic event payloads.
Q000688:
Why this is correct:
CloudWatch Logs show errors, and X-Ray tracing shows where failures and latency occur across calls.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Route 53 checks: availability only.
• S3 access logs: unrelated.
• Config: configuration.

Key takeaway: debug Lambda → logs + traces.
Q000689:
Why this is correct:
sam sync pushes code changes directly to the cloud and does full deployments only when infrastructure changes, speeding iteration.

Why the other options are wrong:
• No difference: sync is faster.
• sam package: packaging only.
• --fast flag: doesn't exist.

Key takeaway: fast dev iteration → sam sync.
Q000690:
Why this is correct:
A stage variable in the integration's function ARN (for example, alias ${stageVariables.alias}) lets each stage call a different alias.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Resource policies redirect: no.
• Hardcode in code: no.
• Separate APIs: duplication.

Key takeaway: per-stage backends → stage variables.
Q000691:
Why this is correct:
Publishing a sample event with the expected source and detail-type to the bus triggers the rule and tests the function end to end.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Trust policy change: not testing.
• No event: doesn't test the rule.
• Wait for production: not testing.

Key takeaway: test rules with sample events.
Q000693:
Why this is correct:
Mocking the third-party API makes tests fast and stable, but real-API integration issues can go undetected.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Removes integration testing: no.
• No error-handling tests: still needed.
• Guarantees production behavior: no.

Key takeaway: mocks trade realism for speed.
Q000694:
Why this is correct:
Manual changes cause drift, so resources no longer match CloudFormation's recorded state and updates can fail.

Why the other options are wrong:
• SAM can't update stacks: it can.
• Deleted stage: different scenario.
• Reserved concurrency: unrelated.

Key takeaway: manual changes → drift → failed deploys.
Q000695:
Why this is correct:
Parameters or mappings supply per-environment values from one template.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Tags on template bucket: no.
• Manual edits: error-prone.
• Three copies: drift.

Key takeaway: one template, many environments → parameters/mappings.
Q000696:
Why this is correct:
A weighted alias splits traffic between two versions (for example, 90/10).

Why the other options are wrong:
• Random second function: unmanaged.
• Usage plan: throttling.
• Layer constraint: dependencies.

Key takeaway: traffic splitting in Lambda → weighted aliases.
Q000697:
Why this is correct:
Immutable, uniquely tagged images (for example, by commit SHA) make each deployment traceable and reproducible.

Why the other options are wrong:
• latest tag: changes underneath.
• Image in env variable: nonsense.
• Disable scanning: unrelated.

Key takeaway: traceable images → unique immutable tags.
Q000699:
Why this is correct:
A change set previews exactly which resources will be added, modified, or replaced before executing.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Stack policy: protects resources.
• Drift report: compares current state.
• Nested stack: structure.

Key takeaway: preview updates → change sets.
Q000700:
Why this is correct:
SAM is a CloudFormation transform: its shorthand expands into standard CloudFormation resources at deployment.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Containers only: no.
• CloudFormation can't deploy Lambda: it can.
• Replaces CloudFormation: uses it.

Key takeaway: SAM = CloudFormation extension.
Q000701:
Why this is correct:
Create a deployment of the tested API configuration and associate it with the prod stage.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Delete test stage: unnecessary.
• Recreate API: unnecessary.
• Change protocol: unrelated.

Key takeaway: promote via deployments to stages.
Q000703:
Why this is correct:
Test commands go in buildspec.yml phases (pre_build or build), so CodeBuild runs them on every commit.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Lambda env vars: no.
• Bucket policy: no.
• Stage description: no.

Key takeaway: CI tests → buildspec phases.
Q000704:
Why this is correct:
$LATEST can change at any time, so test results aren't reproducible. Test a published version (via an alias).

Why the other options are wrong:
• Alias can't point to $LATEST: it can.
• $LATEST can't be invoked: it can.
• Versions can't be invoked: they can.

Key takeaway: test immutable versions.
Q000705:
Why this is correct:
Tests failing in one environment because of hardcoded IDs should read resource IDs from each environment's stack outputs.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Disable stage: avoids the problem.
• Merge environments: loses isolation.
• Admin permissions: unrelated.

Key takeaway: environment-specific values → stack outputs.
Q000707:
Why this is correct:
A custom domain name in API Gateway with an ACM certificate, plus a Route 53 alias record, serves the API at api.example.com.

Why the other options are wrong:
• WAF: security.
• Rename the stage: not a domain.
• S3 policy: unrelated.

Key takeaway: friendly API URL → custom domain.
Q000708:
Why this is correct:
Blue/green switches traffic to a separate new environment. Canary shifts a small portion of traffic to the new version first.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Canary replaces infrastructure: no.
• Same technique: no.
• Service-specific: both apply broadly.

Key takeaway: blue/green = switch; canary = gradual sample.
Q000710:
Why this is correct:
A manual approval stage before production pauses the pipeline until someone approves.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Lambda without permissions: no.
• API resource policy: no.
• Artifacts section: packaging.

Key takeaway: human gate → manual approval action.
Q000711:
Why this is correct:
When an associated alarm fires, CodeDeploy stops the deployment and rolls traffic back to the previous version (if configured).

Why the other options are wrong:
• Ignores alarm: no.
• Pauses indefinitely: no.
• Deletes the function: no.

Key takeaway: alarms trigger automatic rollback.
Q000713:
Why this is correct:
By default, a failed stack update rolls back to the previous working state.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Half-updated forever: no.
• Marks success: no.
• Deletes stack: no.

Key takeaway: CloudFormation updates are transactional.
Q000714:
Why this is correct:
CodeDeploy's ECS compute platform performs blue/green deployments with traffic shifting between task sets.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Config, Trusted Advisor, Inspector: not deployment tools.

Key takeaway: ECS blue/green → CodeDeploy.
Q000715:
Why this is correct:
Canary shifts a small portion once, then the rest. Linear shifts in equal steps over time, which is slower but more gradual.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Linear can't roll back: it can.
• Canary EC2-only: available for Lambda and ECS.
• Same total time: differs.

Key takeaway: canary = two steps; linear = many steps.
Q000718:
Why this is correct:
AllowTraffic failures usually mean instances fail load balancer health checks. Check CodeDeploy events and target group health status.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Flow logs: rarely first.
• CloudTrail for pipeline role: unrelated.
• Bucket access logs: unrelated.

Key takeaway: AllowTraffic failures → target health.
Q000719:
Why this is correct:
X-Ray tracing with subsegment timings shows which downstream call makes processing exceed limits, causing DLQ arrivals.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Trusted Advisor: no.
• Contributor Insights: top contributors, not timing.
• Logs Insights counts: no timing breakdown.

Key takeaway: find slow steps → X-Ray subsegments.
Q000721:
Why this is correct:
A red node in the service map shows the downstream service returning errors or faults, indicating it's the bottleneck.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Throttling API Gateway: not implied.
• Sampling misconfigured: no.
• Client memory leak: unrelated.

Key takeaway: service map colors show where errors originate.
Q000722:
Why this is correct:
Enabling API Gateway execution logging and correlating by request ID reveals malformed Lambda responses that cause 502s.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Retry: hides the bug.
• More memory: unlikely cause.
• Delete logs: loses evidence.

Key takeaway: 502 from Lambda proxy → inspect execution logs.
Q000723:
Why this is correct:
Filter statusCode >= 500, count by endpoint, sort descending, and limit to find the endpoint with the most 5xx errors.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Sort by status: not counts.
• Average status: meaningless.
• Regex on endpoint: wrong field.

Key takeaway: top errors → filter + stats count + sort.
Q000725:
Why this is correct:
EMF metrics are extracted from logs asynchronously, avoiding PutMetricData calls and their latency and throttling.

Why the other options are wrong:
• More dimensions: not the main benefit.
• Creates alarms: no.
• Only 1-second method: no.

Key takeaway: Lambda metrics → EMF.
Q000726:
Why this is correct:
API Gateway execution logs show the authorizer's result and policy, explaining 403 responses.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Config history: no.
• Backend logs: requests never reached it.
• S3 access logs: unrelated.

Key takeaway: authorizer denials → execution logs.
Q000730:
Why this is correct:
Annotations are indexed key-value pairs you can filter traces by. Metadata isn't indexed.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Indexed identically: no.
• Metadata indexed: reversed.
• Subsegments only: no.

Key takeaway: searchable trace data → annotations.
Q000731:
Why this is correct:
Structured JSON logs let Logs Insights discover fields automatically, so you can filter and aggregate reliably.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Automatic compression: no.
• Automatic CMK encryption: no.
• No retention policy: still needed.

Key takeaway: structured logs → queryable fields.
Q000732:
Why this is correct:
The container health check determines liveness and triggers restarts. The target group health check determines readiness to receive traffic.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Same purpose: different.
• Swapped roles: incorrect.
• Scale-in driver: no.

Key takeaway: liveness vs. readiness.
Q000733:
Why this is correct:
Composite alarms page on combined root symptoms, and anomaly detection avoids static thresholds that fire during normal variation.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Shorter periods: more noise.
• SNS per datapoint: more noise.
• Disable after hours: dangerous.

Key takeaway: reduce paging noise → composite + anomaly detection.
Q000735:
Why this is correct:
Publishing with StorageResolution = 1 creates a high-resolution metric usable for alarms with 10-second periods.

Why the other options are wrong:
• All metrics 1-second: default is 60.
• Logs Insights only: no.
• X-Ray: unrelated.

Key takeaway: seconds-level alarms → high-resolution metrics.
Q000736:
Why this is correct:
The health check should confirm startup dependencies (such as the cache) are ready before the task receives traffic.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Remove health check: unsafe.
• Lower CPU: slower.
• Idle timeout: unrelated.

Key takeaway: health checks should reflect readiness.
Q000738:
Why this is correct:
Reserved concurrency set below demand causes throttling during spikes. Raise it or remove the cap.

Why the other options are wrong:
• High memory: doesn't cause throttling.
• Unsupported runtime: different error.
• Missing permission: AccessDenied, not throttling.

Key takeaway: throttling → concurrency limits.
Q000739:
Why this is correct:
AWS Lambda Power Tuning runs the function at several memory sizes and compares cost and duration.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Provisioned concurrency: cold starts.
• Max memory always cheapest: not always.
• Trusted Advisor: not this.

Key takeaway: optimize memory → Power Tuning.
Q000740:
Why this is correct:
A subscription filter matching FATAL streams those events to the Lambda function in near real time.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Scheduled queries: delayed.
• S3 export notifications: delayed.
• X-Ray sampling: traces.

Key takeaway: stream matching logs → subscription filters.
Q000742:
Why this is correct:
Performance Insights shows top SQL and wait events during peaks. Optimize those queries or indexes first.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Disable it: loses insight.
• Delete slow logs: hides problems.
• Bigger instance first: may not fix bad queries.

Key takeaway: diagnose before scaling.
Q000743:
Why this is correct:
API Gateway caches per stage in the API's Region. CloudFront caches at edge locations near users.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Reversed: incorrect.
• CloudFront can't front APIs: it can.
• Identical: different scope.

Key takeaway: Regional cache vs. edge cache.
Q002093:
Why this is correct:
SQS standard is at-least-once, so the same message can arrive twice. An idempotent handler (for example, a conditional write on a payment ID) prevents double charges.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Faster runtime: doesn't prevent duplicates.
• Batch size 1: duplicates still possible.
• Retention period: unrelated.

Key takeaway: at-least-once delivery → idempotency.
Q002094:
Why this is correct:
Optimistic locking with a version attribute and a condition expression rejects writes based on stale data.

Why the other options are wrong:
• BatchWriteItem: no conditions.
• Strong reads: don't prevent concurrent writes.
• Streams: detect after the fact.

Key takeaway: lost updates → optimistic locking.
Q002095:
Why this is correct:
A GSI with customerId as partition key (and a sort attribute) enables the new query, and GSI queries are eventually consistent.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Add LSI later: only at creation.
• GSI shares partition key: no.
• Scan as efficient: no.

Key takeaway: new access pattern → GSI.
Q002096:
Why this is correct:
ReportBatchItemFailures lets the function return only failed message IDs, so successful messages aren't reprocessed.

Why the other options are wrong:
• FIFO: doesn't solve partial failures.
• Delete all first: loses failed messages.
• 12-hour timeout: delays retries.

Key takeaway: partial batch failures → ReportBatchItemFailures.
Q002097:
Why this is correct:
Step Functions Express workflows handle very high event rates for short workflows at low cost.

Why the other options are wrong:
• AWS Batch: batch jobs.
• Standard workflows: lower throughput and higher cost for this rate.
• Custom scheduler on EC2: operations burden.

Key takeaway: high-volume short workflows → Express.
Q002098:
Why this is correct:
An HTTP API JWT authorizer with the Cognito user pool as issuer validates tokens without custom code.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Custom Lambda authorizer: unnecessary code.
• API keys: not user authentication.
• SigV4 in browser: requires AWS credentials.

Key takeaway: Cognito JWTs → JWT authorizer.
Q002099:
Why this is correct:
KMS Encrypt handles only 4 KB. Envelope encryption generates a data key, encrypts the 5 MB file locally, and stores the encrypted key with it.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Quota increase: not possible.
• Asymmetric key: same limits.
• 4 KB chunks: slow and costly.

Key takeaway: large data → envelope encryption.
Q002100:
Why this is correct:
Caching the secret with a TTL (the Parameters and Secrets Lambda Extension or a caching client) cuts API calls and latency while still picking up rotations.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Hardcode in env var: loses rotation.
• Package: insecure.
• More memory: doesn't reduce calls.

Key takeaway: frequent secret reads → cache with TTL.
Q002101:
Why this is correct:
A short-lived presigned URL lets the browser upload directly to S3 without passing large files through API Gateway and Lambda.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Public write: insecure.
• Through API Gateway: payload limits.
• Embedded key: insecure.

Key takeaway: browser uploads → presigned URLs.
Q002102:
Why this is correct:
With Lambda proxy integration, the function must return Access-Control-Allow-Origin in its response. Console CORS covers only the preflight.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Caching: unrelated.
• Timeout: different error.
• API key: unrelated to CORS.

Key takeaway: proxy integration → CORS headers from the function.
Q002103:
Why this is correct:
sam sync --watch detects changes and pushes code updates quickly, avoiding full CloudFormation deployments for each edit.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Timeout: unrelated.
• Recreate stack: slower.
• --no-execute-changeset: doesn't deploy.

Key takeaway: fast iteration → sam sync --watch.
Q002104:
Why this is correct:
Immutable deployments launch new instances in a temporary group, keep full capacity, and roll back by terminating the new instances if they fail.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Rolling with batch: rollback is slower.
• All at once: downtime.
• Rolling: reduced capacity.

Key takeaway: full capacity + clean rollback → immutable.
Q002105:
Why this is correct:
Exporting subnet IDs from the network stack and importing them with Fn::ImportValue shares values, and exports in use can't be changed or deleted.

Why the other options are wrong:
• GetAtt across stacks: not supported.
• Parameters copied: stale.
• Mappings: static.

Key takeaway: cross-stack sharing → Export/ImportValue.
Q002106:
Why this is correct:
Container images support up to 10 GB, enough for large ML libraries.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Higher compression: unzipped limit still applies.
• Five layers: 250 MB total unzipped limit.
• Ephemeral storage: /tmp, not package size.

Key takeaway: large dependencies → container images.
Q002107:
Why this is correct:
Adding customerId as an X-Ray annotation indexes it, so traces can be filtered by that value.

Why the other options are wrong:
• stdout only: not in traces.
• Metadata: not searchable.
• Segment name: misuse.

Key takeaway: searchable traces → annotations.
Q002108:
Why this is correct:
Reserved concurrency on the order function guarantees it capacity that other functions can't consume.

Why the other options are wrong:
• More memory: doesn't reserve capacity.
• Provisioned concurrency on reporting: doesn't protect orders.
• Longer timeout: unrelated.

Key takeaway: protect critical functions → reserved concurrency.
Q002109:
Why this is correct:
Lambda Power Tuning measures duration and cost across memory sizes. CPU-bound functions often get cheaper with more memory.

Why the other options are wrong:
• X-Ray sets memory: no.
• Minimum memory always cheapest: false.
• 15-minute timeout: unrelated.

Key takeaway: test memory settings empirically.
Q002110:
Why this is correct:
Write-through updates the cache when prices change, and a TTL limits staleness for anything missed.

Why the other options are wrong:
• No TTL: stale forever.
• Disable caching: loses performance.
• Bigger node: doesn't fix staleness.

Key takeaway: freshness → write-through + TTL.
Q002111:
Why this is correct:
A Logs Insights query with stats count(*) by errorCode, sorted, finds the most frequent errors quickly.

Why the other options are wrong:
• S3 export and script: slow.
• CloudTrail: API calls.
• Monitor tab: no grouping by error code.

Key takeaway: aggregate log errors → Logs Insights stats.
